site_surface.short_summary: Blue-red Ravnican guild of elemental science, civic engineering, volatile invention, and crisis-scale experimentation under the long shadow of Niv-Mizzet and Ral Zarek.
site_surface.one_sentence_identity: The Izzet League turns curiosity into machinery, spells, public works, and occasionally city-shaking disasters.
best_for: users who learn by building prototypes
users who enjoy creative problem solving
users who value invention and discovery
users who can tolerate failed experiments
content_warnings_or_sensitivity_notes: Placement interpretation should avoid glorifying recklessness in real-world safety contexts.

core_identity.summary: The Izzet League is the blue-red guild of Ravnica: a dragon-led culture of elemental magic, mizzium technology, civic engineering, and volatile discovery. The expanded story pass adds concrete examples of this identity at multiple levels: Trenz on Experiment Day, Madarrak and Castan pursuing Erno Zslod, lower-rank attendants fighting for recognition, and Ral Zarek directing crisis-scale resonator and beacon operations.
unknowns: The ultimate purpose of the Return to Ravnica-era dangerous experimental push is stated as unknown in the reviewed official guide.
The full current post-Murders at Karlov Manor internal leadership state beyond Ral's 2023 guildmaster reference was not fully established in the reviewed official sources.

structure.summary: The guild is strongly shaped by Niv-Mizzet's intellect, compartmentalized planning, and project-driven research culture. Known roles include chemisters, blastseekers, and attendants; known internal groups include the Izmundi, Izmagnus, and engineered weirds.

known_roles.description: Alchemist role that forges mizzium and other elements into arcane tools and experiments with alloys, energies, and runic markings.
Mage role that wields and controls arcane tools created by chemisters.
Support role that records and organizes information, acquires rare materials, and completes experiments under dangerous circumstances.
Izzet-associated worker or role mentioned around Nivix in The Gathering Storm: Chapter 17; exact duties were not defined in the reviewed passage.
Project leadership role held by Ral Zarek during Project Lightning Bug.
Izzet specialist role represented by Kelen Jek’s trial proposal in Paper Trail.

great_tension.summary: The Izzet great tension is invention as public benefit versus invention as obsession: the same guild that builds infrastructure and emergency solutions also rewards breakthroughs, speed, and spectacle strongly enough that risky or ethically compromised experiments can emerge under pressure.
great_tension.interpretation_warning: This summarizes a pattern across official guide text and inspected story examples; it is not a direct psychological statement from Wizards.

historical_timeline.event: The Izzet League's original mandate is to solve civic public works problems.
historical_timeline.date_or_era: Original guild mandate / ancient Ravnica context
historical_timeline.notes: Exact date not independently asserted beyond parun-era context in reviewed claims.

historical_timeline.event: Return to Ravnica-era guide presents Niv-Mizzet driving the Izzet into deeper dangerous experimental magic for an unknown purpose.
Guilds of Ravnica-era guidance describes Niv-Mizzet as leader in name and spirit while Ral Zarek handles day-to-day operations.
During War of the Spark, the Izzet League is shown under Master Zarek and Chamberlain Maree during the crisis, with Niv-Mizzet dead before Operation Desperation.
Operation Desperation seeks to resurrect Niv-Mizzet as the new Living Guildpact, with Niv-Mizzet stepping down as Izzet guildmaster if successful.
During the Phyrexian invasion of Ravnica, Ral Zarek is referred to as Izzet guildmaster.
historical_timeline.date_or_era: March of the Machine / Phyrexian invasion

historical_timeline.event: During the Phyrexian invasion, some Izzet defend Ravnica while others are drawn toward New Phyrexia's perceived technological opportunities.
historical_timeline.date_or_era: March of the Machine / Phyrexian invasion

historical_timeline.event: After the Phyrexian invasion, official guidance says much of Ravnica's rebuilding is spearheaded by the Izzet as they set aside wild destructive experiments for reconstruction and public works.
Trenz’s Experiment Day shows Niv-Mizzet-directed Izzet research producing useful discoveries and destructive side effects.
Madarrak and Castan pursued Erno Zslod and recovered a mizzium-related device connected to a teleportation experiment.
Paper Trail documents an Izzet mizzium augmentation proposal whose consequences intersected with Golgari and Simic material.
Testing the Dark Waters depicts lower-rank Izzet advancement pressure, unsanctioned lab work, and ethically compromised experimentation.
Ral Zarek directed the Nivix-centered resonator network under emergency conditions; the network failed catastrophically after a surge from the Azorius-side node.
historical_timeline.date_or_era: The Gathering Storm / pre-War of the Spark

historical_timeline.event: Niv-Mizzet entrusted Ral Zarek with the beacon mission and personally delayed Nicol Bolas during the invasion.

historical_timeline.event: Ral Zarek activated the Interplanar Beacon after fighting through Bolas-controlled opposition.

mechanics.rules_summary: A replicate cost may be paid any number of times as an additional cost; when the spell is cast, it is copied for each time the replicate cost was paid.
mechanics.design_or_flavor_connection: Official guild kit guidance identifies replicate as the original Ravnica-block Izzet mechanic and connects it to Izzet's spell-scaling identity.

mechanics.rules_summary: A spell can be cast for its overload cost; if paid, its text changes instances of target to each and the spell does not require targets.
mechanics.design_or_flavor_connection: Official mechanics guidance identifies overload as the Return to Ravnica Izzet League mechanic and frames it as powering up instants and sorceries to large proportions.

mechanics.rules_summary: A player may cast an instant or sorcery card from their graveyard by discarding a card as an additional cost; if cast this way, the card is exiled when it leaves the stack.
mechanics.design_or_flavor_connection: Official mechanics and guild kit guidance identify jump-start as the Guilds of Ravnica Izzet mechanic and connect it to getting a second chance at spells.

mechanics.rules_summary: Not a formal card keyword in this profile; represents story technology involving mizzium frameworks, suits, coils, batteries, and devices.
mechanics.design_or_flavor_connection: Story evidence makes mizzium a useful search and placement signal for Izzet applied invention.
mechanics.notes: Not a game mechanic; stored here as lore technology metadata.

mechanics.rules_summary: Not a formal game mechanic; story-scale Izzet/Guildpact engineering system.
mechanics.design_or_flavor_connection: Represents Izzet crisis engineering at city scale and supports placement around volatile scaling.
